entry_state: The literature supplies scoped accounting structures, provenance, partial-identification methods, rule languages, extraction tools and solvers. None alone supplies the complete disclosure-to-history-to-event-to-journal argument. Integration, a fair typed-library comparison and empirical advantage remain to be established; the next chapter must explain the proposed architecture and its division of responsibilities.
exit_state: The architecture places a shared typed representation between evidence and multiple authoring methods. AccDSL retains accounting, time, uncertainty and execution semantics; narrow adapters return typed results. The DSL remains a reversible authoring choice, and the next mathematical chapter must define the compatible histories and future outcomes carried by this architecture.
findings: Figure 5.1 connects evidence, representation, histories, execution and results while retaining assumptions; the borrowing-100 example separates an assumed 60/40 split from a reported fact.
The comparison keeps typed Python/schema/SQL capable of the whole product. Shared conformance and a reversible frontend decision are explicit.
The component table is a reference comparison with a repeated header across pages 82–83. Source inspection, dependency pinning, licence observations and executed integration remain distinct.
Contract, valuation, solver and language-model responses have explicit limits; none can silently take over accounting recognition or committed journal meaning. No confirmed new defect.
